Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

In extension menu > Preferences > Link handling, the toggle called “Open links in background” is on. It controls links opened from the reading queue only: new tabs stay in the same window and don't take focus. It doesn't change what happens when someone clicks links on ordinary web pages or browser bookmarks. If the extension isn't enabled in private windows, this preference doesn't apply there either. Don't imply the toggle controls all browser links or changes tab order. Put the location of the preference near the beginning and explain its exact scope in plain language. It may help to separate what the setting does from what it doesn't. Last assessment from support review: the preference behaves as designed for reading-queue links; normal-page links are outside its scope, and this report alone doesn't show a defect. Keep this assessment at the end. Don't add troubleshooting or recommendations, and don't make claims about bookmarks beyond the scope described here.", "output": "Write a clear internal update for the support team, not a customer reply, using the notes below. Use plain language and put the setting’s location near the beginning. Explain what the preference does and does not control, and keep the final assessment as the last section.

Cedar Tabs is a browser extension, version 4.2. The “Open links in background” toggle is on under extension menu > Preferences > Link handling. It applies only to links opened from the reading queue: new tabs remain in the same window and do not take focus. It does not change how links opened from ordinary web pages or browser bookmarks behave. If the extension is not enabled in private windows, the preference does not apply there either.

A user reported that a link from a normal page still replaced the current tab and asked whether the toggle was broken. A check found that a reading-queue link opened in the background as expected, while a normal-page link replaced the current tab. Do not suggest that the toggle controls all browser links or changes tab order. Make no claims about bookmarks beyond the stated scope, and do not add troubleshooting steps or recommendations.

End with this support review assessment: “The preference behaves as designed for reading-queue links; normal-page links are outside its scope, and this report alone doesn't show a defect.”"}]
